steps.body: The **domain** is the set of inputs; the **range** is the set of outputs. For the pairs (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6), the domain is {1, 2, 3} and the range is {2, 4, 6}. Inputs on the left, outputs on the right.

widget.prompt: For the pairs (1,5), (2,7), (3,9), what is the range?

options.feedback: Yes — the range is the set of outputs (second numbers).
That's the domain (the inputs). The range is the outputs: {5, 7, 9}.
The range is only the outputs, not every number: {5, 7, 9}.

explanationVariants: All three outputs are 3, and a set lists each value once: {3}.
The range is the set of outputs, so just {3}.

widget.prompt: For the pairs (0,3), (1,3), (2,3), what is the range?

commonBuilds.feedback: That's the domain (the inputs). The outputs are all 3, so the range is {3}.
The range is only the outputs: they're all 3, so {3}.

widget.missFeedback: Range = the OUTPUTS (second numbers); a set lists a repeated value once: {3}.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — every output is 3, and a set lists it once.

steps.body: A relation is a **function** when each input has exactly one output. (1, 2), (1, 5) is NOT a function — input 1 has two different outputs. Repeated outputs are fine; repeated inputs are not.

widget.prompt: Which set of pairs is a function?

options.feedback: Yes — every input (1, 2, 3) appears once, so each has exactly one output.
Input 1 maps to both 2 and 3, so this isn't a function.
Input 5 maps to both 1 and 2, so this isn't a function.

steps.body: On a graph, the **vertical line test** checks this: if any vertical line crosses the graph more than once, that x-value has two outputs, so it's not a function. One crossing per vertical line means it passes.

widget.prompt: Sweep the vertical line across the circle. Record the greatest number of crossings, then decide whether it is a function.
widget.successFeedback: Two crossings over most of the sweep, so it is not a function: an input with two outputs breaks the rule. The test is not a convention — it is the definition, drawn.
widget.moreSweepFeedback: Keep sweeping. One position proves nothing; the verdict depends on the worst case anywhere along the domain.
widget.verdictFeedback: Look again at the maximum crossing count you recorded. Two outputs for one input means not a function.

explanationVariants: The inputs 2, 4, 6 are all different, so each has one output — a function.
Repeated outputs (all 1) are fine; the inputs are distinct, so it's a function.

widget.prompt: For the pairs (2,1), (4,1), (6,1), is it a function?

options.label: Yes — each input has one output
options.feedback: Yes — inputs 2, 4, 6 are distinct; repeated outputs don't matter.

options.label: No — the outputs repeat
options.feedback: Repeated outputs are allowed. What matters is that each input appears once — and they do.

options.label: No — there are too few points
options.feedback: The number of points doesn't matter; distinct inputs make it a function.

explanationVariants: The domain is the set of inputs (first numbers): {1, 2, 3}.
Inputs are 1, 2, 3, so the domain is {1, 2, 3}.

The domain is only the inputs: {1, 2, 3}.

explanationVariants: In (4,1), (4,2), (5,3), input 4 maps to both 1 and 2 — not a function.
The repeated input 4 with different outputs breaks the function rule.

widget.prompt: Which set of pairs is NOT a function?

options.feedback: Yes — input 4 has two outputs (1 and 2), so it's not a function.
Every input is distinct here, so this IS a function.
Distinct inputs with a repeated output is still a function.

Check whether that repeated input has two different outputs.

steps.body: Domain is inputs, range is outputs; one output per input makes a function.
takeaways: Domain = set of inputs; range = set of outputs.
A function gives each input exactly one output.
Repeated outputs are fine; repeated inputs (with different outputs) are not.
